subject: literature
passage: Every morning, Joaquim opened his newspaper kiosk on a corner in Lisbon before the shops around it had raised their shutters. He stacked the papers in neat piles and set a small radio on the ______ time the first customers, mostly delivery drivers and early commuters, arrived, he had already read the sports pages twice. He liked that quiet hour more than any other part of the day.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "He stacked the papers in neat piles and set a small radio on the counter" is a complete sentence. "By the time the first customers … arrived" is an introductory phrase for the next independent clause, "he had already read the sports pages twice." A period is needed between the two sentences.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This choice attaches "by the time the first customers … arrived" to the first sentence, leaving "he had already read …" joined by only a comma: a comma splice.
explanation.B: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together.
explanation.C: Incorrect. When "and" joins two independent clauses, a comma is needed before it.
explanation.D: Correct. A period ends the first sentence, and "By the time …" begins the second.
